processing_steps.atmosphere: toluene as process control reagent (to avoid oxidation)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Milled in planetary ball mill (Model no. PM 400/2, Retsch) at 200 rpm; ball to powder ratio 10:1; tungsten carbide (WC) vials and WC balls; milling stopped intermittently for 20 min after every 1 h to avoid overheating.

structures.overall_structure: Multiphase solid solution formed after 25 h of milling: BCC (ferrite, major phase) + γ-brass type + trace amount of undissolved Si; nanocrystalline.

characterization_methods.technique: High resolution X-ray diffraction (XRD) with Rietveld refinement
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EMPYREAN, PANALYTICAL; Co-Kα source; operating voltage 40 kV; current 40 mA; scan rate 5° min⁻¹
characterization_methods.purpose: To study the alloying behavior/phase evolution during milling and to determine the lattice parameter, phase fraction, crystallite size, microstrain and dislocation density of the 25 h milled powder.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Solid solution formed after 25 h of milling: BCC (a = 0.286 nm) + γ-brass type (a = 0.872 nm) + trace Si; refined with GoF = 1.08 and χ² = 1.18.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Background fitted with Chebyschev-I background function with 10 coefficients; peak profiles fitted from broadening of Lorentzian and Gaussian component of pseudo-Voigt profile function; average crystallite size and isotropic microstrain based on uniaxial model; least-square minimization to achieve acceptable goodness of fit.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Goodness of fit for the 25 h refinement: GoF = 1.08, χ² = 1.18

analytical_models.equation_role: ρ_dd = (3√(2π) <ε²>^½) / (t·b), where b = (√3/2)a for BCC, t = crystallite size in nm, a = lattice parameter in nm, ε = microstrain
analytical_models.model_note: Used to calculate the BCC dislocation density (1.94 × 10¹⁸ m⁻²) of the 25 h milled powder.

analytical_models.equation_role: β = 4ε tanθ, where β is FWHM and θ is the Bragg angle
analytical_models.model_note: Used to obtain the microstrain of each phase of the 25 h milled powder (Table 2).

unmapped_findings: The solid solution has been formed after 25 h of milling; the phases formed are BCC (a = 0.286 nm; JCPDS# 00-006-0696) and γ-brass type (a = 0.872 nm; JCPDS# 01-078-2831). Milling was extended to 35 h for further nanostructuring (b0038).

Alloying with milling time is related to diffusion of low-melting-point elements into the matrix of higher-melting-point elements; Al has the highest alloying rate (its XRD intensity diminishes after 15 h), and after 20 h the intense Ni and Mn peaks are no longer evident (b0038).
The crystallite size of Si decreased from 20 nm (25 h) to 14 nm (35 h) as milling extended (b0040).
The lattice parameter of the major BCC phase formed during milling is close to ferritic iron (α-Fe) acting as the host lattice (b0058).
